rulings.evidence: The source names no shape, so the generic dry short-cut pasta id is the honest match rather than rotini specifically; board carries `pasta` 7 of 7 at 0.0571. Source states its own 300 g.
'Medium' is a size word: the 'medium yellow onion' -> onions ruling of 2026-08-26 transfers directly, board 7 of 7. Medium onion weighed at 110 g, between the estate's 70 g small and a large.
Turmeric measured by the teaspoon is the ground spice jar, not fresh root: not a form flip but a rename, the same call as 'ground oregano' -> dried-oregano. Board 7 of 7; 1/2 tsp ground = 1.5 g.

REFUSED both near rows: the board's `butter` match is dairy butter (a wrong-food match) and peanut-butter is a different nut at roughly a third of the price. No estate id names an almond spread, so it goes to the registrar. 2 tbsp = 32 g.

new_commodity_proposals.evidence: A nut spread sold in the nut-butter aisle at roughly three times peanut butter per jar, and nutritionally distinct (614 cal, 21 g protein, 55.5 g fat per 100 g). The only near ids are `butter` (dairy, an outright wrong food that the board's matcher offered) and `peanut-butter` (a different nut and a different price class), so no existing id prices this food under another spelling. Not a form flip of anything: there is no other almond spread on the board.
